reason: §14.8 (6018, 6022..6035) makes gaia-core implement an allowlist for unhealthy bodies: 11 operations. §16.7.2 carries the freeze gate as a field of the object itself — SoulTransferFreeze.permitted_operations_sorted at 6639 — with its content fixed at 6646..6662: 13 operations. The two lists differ. Freeze-only: InspectTransferState, SubmitTransferDispute, SubmitTransferResolutionEvidence, FinalizeTransferWhenAuthorized. Health-only: SubmitRecoveryProof, ReadBankDataRequiredForRecovery. Shared: 9. No line states how the gates compose when a body is both frozen and unhealthy. The lines mentioning either gate are 5904, 6018, 6020, 6023, 7252, 11113, 13418, 13435, 13869, 15382 and 15874; none of them poses the conjunction. Consequence: FinalizeTransferWhenAuthorized is permitted by the freeze gate and forbidden by the health gate, and SubmitRecoveryProof the other way. An implementer must invent whether composition is intersection or union. Under intersection a frozen Soul on an unhealthy body can never finalize, and the agreement finalization_deadline fixed at 6584 passes with no defined outcome.

decision.rule: For a body that is both under transfer freeze and not healthy, the permitted set is the INTERSECTION of the two allowlists: ReadStoredObjects, VerifyObjects, InspectTemporalHealth, SynchronizeClock, RequestTimeAttestation, RespondToTimeChallenge, RequestRevalidation, FetchRecoveryMaterial, ReceiveReinstatementProof (nine operations).
decision.why: 6018 and 6648 are both stated as allowlists ("許可されるのは次の操作だけである"), so membership is a necessary condition, not an offer. Two necessary conditions compose by conjunction. The union reading would let a frozen unhealthy body submit a recovery proof (health-only) while frozen, or submit a transfer dispute (freeze-only) while unhealthy, breaching the other gate. 6018 also states the floor directly: an unhealthy body must advance no normal Gaia state, and adding freeze can only restrict further.

subject: a CoreOperationRequest that violates the §14.8 health gate and also violates a step the 14147 order does place, such as an expired SessionBinding or an invalid authority lease
observed: the specification does not determine which rejection code is returned, because the health gate has no position in the mandated order
reason: Line 14147 mandates the order in which a state-changing CoreOperation runs its validations, "at least" thirteen numbered steps. Transfer freeze is placed: step (4) lists Soul identity, DeviceIncarnation, lease, trust epoch, transfer freeze, AuthorityOperationHeader and operation sequence. The health gate is not placed. §14.8 (6018) makes gaia-core apply an allowlist for degraded, unhealthy, quarantined, excluded and revalidation_pending bodies, and 13435 requires that gate to be applied consistently across CLI, API, daemon, SDK, signer, object creation and relay — but none of the thirteen steps names health or TemporalHealth. CommunicationHealthAttachment scope and epoch matching (6060, 13418, 15874) are likewise absent from the thirteen steps. "At least" permits insertion but fixes no position, so when a health violation and a listed violation both hold, the specification does not determine which reject code is emitted. Consequence: two implementations that insert the health gate at different points return different rejection codes for the same CoreOperationRequest, and the offline-verification claim in §23.20 depends on rejection being determined by the specification rather than by the implementation.
verification: confirmed gap after a whole-specification search: Read the 13-step order at 14147: step (4) lists transfer freeze but no health/TemporalHealth gate; 13435 and 15874 require the gate to be applied consistently but fix no position. Searched 健康/TemporalHealth/CommunicationHealthAttachment near the order.

decision.rule: The section 14.8 health gate is evaluated inside step (4) of the 14147 order, jointly with the authority and lease checks, and BEFORE the transfer-freeze check within that step. When a request violates both the health gate and another step, the emitted reject belongs to the health gate family.
decision.why: Step (4) is the subject-state step: Soul identity, DeviceIncarnation, lease, trust epoch, transfer freeze. Health is a subject-state property of exactly that kind. It precedes the freeze check because 6018 bars every state-advancing operation for an unhealthy body while freeze bars only a named family, and a bar on everything must be evaluated before a bar on a subset or the reject code would name the narrower cause.

subject: the Stripe transfer life-cycle transitions (success, available, failed, reversal) appended to an existing BeneficiaryTransferRecord
reason: §18.18.7 is decomposed into Core Operations step by step: its step 3 is InitiateBeneficiaryTransfer and its step 8 is RecordBeneficiaryPayout, so its numbered steps are operations. Its step 7 (line 8895) appends the transfer’s own life-cycle transitions to `BeneficiaryTransferRecord`, which is acceptance of an external result plus a state change under line 14029. No row owns it: InitiateBeneficiaryTransfer only creates the record (stated `submitted` at 8894), RecordBeneficiaryPayout owns `BeneficiaryPayoutReceipt`, and ProcessPaymentCallback’s result_object_classes are `PaymentReceipt`/`PaymentSettlement`/`PayoutEntitlement`.

decision.rule: A Core Operation `RecordBeneficiaryTransferTransition` must exist, under Payment-Service authority, whose result object class is `BeneficiaryTransferRecord`, whose external dependency class is `stripe_payout`, and whose reject-code family is `transfer`; the step at 8895 binds it instead of remaining a sub-step.
decision.why: 8895 requires appending the transfer’s own transitions to `BeneficiaryTransferRecord`; 8891 and 8896 place the neighbouring steps of the same numbered procedure on Core Operations, so the registry already treats this procedure as operation-level. The transitions are external Stripe results, which line 14029 lists as a limb of the predicate, and the append is a protocol state change.
decision.override: If a later reading shows line 8895 is inside the same operation as 8896 — that recording the payout receipt and appending the transfer transition are one act under one authority — then RecordBeneficiaryPayout’s result_object_classes grow to include `BeneficiaryTransferRecord` and no new row is added.

resolved_by: the Core Operation `RecordBeneficiaryTransferTransition`, added to the registry on 2026-10-08 and bound by the step at spec line 8891. The judgment that fixed the row is the `decision` below; its override condition still governs.

subject: the provider issuing a fresh access credential to the new controller of a transferred StorageContract
reason: §20.6 line 9682 requires that when a `StorageContract`’s controller changes, the provider verify the new controller’s eKYC, SoulTransferFinalization and new authority and then issue a new access credential. Issue of a provider credential is a state change under storage-provider authority, a line-14029 operation, yet no row owns it: the access-grant kinds (IssueContentAccessGrant, RevokeOrGrantContentAccess) are bound to protected-content access with result classes `ContentAccessGrant`/`KeyEnvelope`, IssueStorageReservationGrant and IssueStorageReceipt cover reservations and receipts rather than controller re-binding, and CreateStorageContract creates the contract rather than a credential.

decision.rule: A Core Operation must exist for the provider-issued access credential that line 9682 requires, under `storage_provider_authorization`. Its row cannot be written until the specification names the object the credential is: the line names `StorageContract` as the contract whose customer is unchanged and the credential only as “新しいアクセスcredential”, and no object type of that name is defined in §3.1 or §22.5. The operation is therefore recorded and not invented.
decision.why: 9682 states the act and its three preconditions; 9695 lists what Gaia Storage treats as its validity objects (`StorageReceipt`, `StorageAudit`, canonical manifest, ACL/certificate) and names no access-credential object, so the registry cannot name the result class without inventing one.
decision.override: If §20 or §22.5 is later read to define a credential object — or if the credential is held to be a `StorageContract` state transition rather than a distinct object — the row is written with that class and the step at 9682 binds it.

resolved_by: the Core Operation `IssueStorageAccessCredential`, added to the registry on 2026-10-08 and bound by the step at spec line 9682. The judgment that fixed the row is the `decision` below; its override condition still governs.

subject: the invalidation or decay of a storage contribution after an audit failure
reason: §20.7.6 line 9744 states that an audit failure starts at-risk/repair and revokes or decays the affected contribution, and §24.13 line 13640 repeats it as an observable test condition. Revocation and decay are limbs of the line-14029 predicate and §21 mandates a row for every state-changing act, yet no row owns it: the storage rows cover reservation grants, receipts, availability proofs, challenges, repair and garbage collection, and none changes a contributed-capacity state in response to an audit failure.

decision.rule: A Core Operation must exist that revokes or decays a storage contribution on audit failure, under `storage_provider_authorization`, grounded on line 9744 and observable at line 13640. The step at 9744 binds it instead of remaining a sub-step.
decision.why: 9744 states the effect on the contribution; 13640 repeats it as a condition a conformance test can observe, so the effect is part of the specification’s own testable surface rather than an implementation detail; 13638 shows the contribution is measured in receipts, which the existing receipt and challenge rows create rather than revoke.
decision.override: If a later reading shows the audit failure only stops future accrual — that 9744 is a consequence of StorageAuditResult rather than an act any authority performs — then no row is added and the step stays a sub-step of the audit result.

resolved_by: the Core Operation `RevokeStorageContribution`, added to the registry on 2026-10-08 and bound by the step at spec line 9744. The judgment that fixed the row is the `decision` below; its override condition still governs.
